> no, #126400 is failing in a different test

```
[FAILED] failed to update Service "external-local-update": Internal error occurred: failed to allocate requested HealthCheck NodePort 30202: provided port is already allocated
In [It] at: k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e/network/loadbalancer.go:1616 @ 07/21/24 12:41:29.957
```

From logs we can clearly see that failure is due to nodePort allocation. From this PR we achieving to add retry mechanism to allocate other port if existing port is used by other services.


@danwinship Do you have any suggestions or ideas to keep track of #126400 too ?

> From logs we can clearly see that failure is due to nodePort allocation.

(HealthCheckNodePort actually; not _exactly_ the same thing.)

> From this PR we achieving to add retry mechanism to allocate other port if existing port is used by other services.

This PR changes the _initial_ NodePort allocation to use a port in the static range, so as to guarantee that when we delete the service later, it's not possible that the NodePort is used by other services.

Though of course, once we fix #126400, that guarantee would be broken; if this test and the LB HCNP test ran in parallel, then you could get:

- `"should release NodePorts on delete"`: create service with randomly-selected NodePort 32123 → succeeds because nobody is using that port
- `"should release NodePorts on delete"`: delete service
- `"should handle updates to ExternalTrafficPolicy field"`: create service with randomly-selected HealthCheckNodePort 32123 → succeeds because nobody is using that port
- `"should release NodePorts on delete"`: recreate service with NodePort 32123 → **FAIL**
- `"should handle updates to ExternalTrafficPolicy field"`: delete service
- `"should handle updates to ExternalTrafficPolicy field"`: recreate service with HealthCheckNodePort 32123 → succeeds because nobody is using that port

hmm, the reported issue was also on the loadbalancer tests, and these are the service tests 

this is more involved than I thought

> hmm, the reported issue was also on the loadbalancer tests, and these are the service tests

#125466 is on the service tests (and this PR would fix it). #126400 is on the LB tests, and a similar fix could be made there (and, in isolation, would fix that test), but if you fix both tests in the same way then it gets un-fixed as described above, because both tests might end up picking the same "reserved" nodeport to use.

I think the fix is either:
1. Allocate specific nodeports to different tests statically. So, eg, the service test would always use `(e2eservice.NodePortRange.Base + 12) % e2eservice.NodePortRange.Size` and the LB test would always use `(e2eservice.NodePortRange.Base + 37) % e2eservice.NodePortRange.Size`. We sort of do this with hostports / hostNetwork pod ports, though it's very ad hoc. But this seems less likely to work well with nodeports because there are fewer of them so we're more likely to end up conflicting with something that's an existing part of the cluster the e2e tests are running in...
2. Keep track of reserved nodeports at runtime, `e2eservice.ReserveNodePort()` or something (so then there'd also have to be an `e2eservice` function to request an unused nodeport too). This would be simpler if it was always literally `.NodePort`, but sometimes it's `.HealthCheckNodePort`.

probably 2?

definitively 1. is not possible because of the reasons you mention 

I think we should iterate in 2.

/close

Thanks for your reply. Okay makes sense, then I will post a PR with functionality
-  to `Reserve` and `Unreserve` nodeports. and
-  In case any  service is created/updated and assigned a `reserved`  nodeport, it will be deleted and creation/updation will be retried n times  till it gets a nodeport that is not reserved.

>  with a big comment saying new tests should not use THAT functionality

Do we specifically want to avoid using `Reserve` and `Unreserve` nodeports functions in new tests ? My assumption was that these functions could be useful even in new tests, especially in scenarios where a nodeport is de-allocated and reachability is tested. In such cases, the expected failure of reachability can only be guaranteed if the nodeport isn't allocated to another service.

> I don't think you want to do it this way (calling into a method that creates the service). Particularly given that in one case you're reserving a NodePort an in another case a HealthCheckNodePort.

I was trying to avoid more consumption of these methods, your approach sounds simpler though

Thanks for pointing out the article. Considering only static ports for these two tests would greatly simplify the implementation. I am also considering 
- to combine `e2eservice.GetUnusedStaticNodePort()` and `e2eservice.ReserveStaticNodePort(port)` in order to avoid race between two calls
- moving looping part inside `GetUnusedStaticNodePort()` so that a call to this would return a free port

I will post a PR soon and we can address these implementation details there.
